name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q01 - Historical discovery of live cell and nucleus

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell.
Statement II: Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus in 1831.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim on live cell observation
According to historical records described in the textbook, Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek was the first scientist to observe and describe a live cell under microscope lenses.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim on the discovery of the nucleus
The dense spherical organelle called the nucleus was subsequently discovered and described by the Scottish botanist Robert Brown as early as 1831.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements are factually accurate descriptions of early microscopic discoveries in cell biology.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q02 - De novo origin of cells and organelle presence

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: New cells generate de novo from abiotic non-living materials under natural conditions.
Statement II: Prokaryotic cells possess membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and chloroplasts.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding de novo cell formation
Modern cell theory explicitly rejects spontaneous generation; as established by Rudolf Virchow, all living cells divide and arise exclusively from pre-existing cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding prokaryotic organelle composition
Prokaryotic cells completely lack membrane-delimited internal organelles like mitochondria and chloroplasts, possessing only non-membrane bound 70S ribosomes.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements are scientifically incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q03 - Dimensions and wall characteristics of Mycoplasma

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mycoplasmas are the smallest living cells, measuring only about 0.3 µm in length.
Statement II: Mycoplasmas possess an unusually thick and rigid cellulosic cell wall.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Mycoplasma cell size
Mycoplasmas represent the smallest known living cells and typically measure approximately 0.3 µm in length.

Step 2: Evaluation of Mycoplasma cell wall presence
A defining diagnostic feature of Mycoplasma among prokaryotes is the complete absence of a cell wall surrounding its plasma membrane.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is true, whereas the second statement is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q04 - Reductionist biology and collagen triple helical structure

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The physico-chemical approach to investigate biological processes using cell-free systems is termed Holozoic Biology.
Statement II: G.N. Ramachandran discovered the triple helical structure of collagen published in Nature in 1954.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the terminology for the physico-chemical approach
The scientific approach that applies concepts and methods of physics and chemistry to explain living processes at the molecular level using cell-free systems is called Reductionist Biology, not Holozoic Biology.

Step 2: Evaluation of G.N. Ramachandran's discovery
G.N. Ramachandran elucidated the triple helical structure of collagen, a landmark discovery published in the journal Nature in 1954.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is false, whereas the second statement is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q05 - Foundational observations of Schleiden and Schwann

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Matthias Schleiden observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant.
Statement II: Theodore Schwann concluded that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character of plant cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Matthias Schleiden's botanical studies
In 1838, Matthias Schleiden examined a wide variety of plant tissues and concluded that all plants consist of cells and cellular aggregates that organize into tissues.

Step 2: Evaluation of Theodore Schwann's comparative studies
In 1839, Theodore Schwann studied animal cells and plant tissues, concluding that the presence of an outer cell wall represents an exclusive distinguishing character of plant cells.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements are accurate historical observations that formed the basis of classical cell theory.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q06 - Ribosomal subunit composition and bounding membranes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Ribosomes are granular organelles surrounded by a single unit phospholipid membrane.
Statement II: Eukaryotic 80S ribosomes are composed of 50S and 30S subunits.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the structural boundary of ribosomes
Ribosomes are non-membrane bound ribonucleoprotein complexes found free in the cytoplasm or associated with membranes; they are never enclosed by a membrane.

Step 2: Evaluation of eukaryotic ribosomal subunit values
Eukaryotic cytoplasmic 80S ribosomes are assembled from 60S and 40S subunits, whereas 50S and 30S subunits form the 70S ribosomes of prokaryotes.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements are scientifically incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q07 - Biochemical composition of human erythrocyte membrane

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The membrane of a human erythrocyte has approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids.
Statement II: Lipid molecules in the plasma membrane are arranged with their polar heads facing the hydrophobic inner core.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of human erythrocyte membrane composition
Biochemical analyses of human red blood cell membranes establish that they consist of approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids.

Step 2: Evaluation of phospholipid bilayer orientation
In the lipid bilayer, polar hydrophilic heads are oriented outward towards the aqueous environment, while nonpolar hydrophobic tails face inward.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is true, whereas the second statement is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q08 - Cell wall constituents of algae and higher plants

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The cell wall of algae consists of peptidoglycan, lipopolysaccharides, and teichoic acid.
Statement II: In plants other than algae, the cell wall consists of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of algal cell wall composition
The cell wall of algae is composed of cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals like calcium carbonate, whereas peptidoglycan is characteristic of bacterial envelopes.

Step 2: Evaluation of higher plant cell wall composition
The cell wall in typical plants is constructed of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and structural proteins.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is false, whereas the second statement is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q09 - Morphological classification of metacentric and acrocentric chromosomes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: A metacentric chromosome has a middle centromere forming two equal arms.
Statement II: An acrocentric chromosome has a centromere situated close to its end, forming one extremely short arm and one very long arm.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the structure of metacentric chromosomes
A metacentric chromosome possesses a centromere located centrally along the chromosome axis, dividing it into two equal-length chromatid arms.

Step 2: Evaluation of the structure of acrocentric chromosomes
An acrocentric chromosome has its primary constriction positioned very close to one pole, producing one remarkably shortened arm and one elongated arm.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements accurately describe the morphological criteria used to classify chromosomes based on centromere position.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q10 - Locomotory function of bacterial pili and fimbriae

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Pili and fimbriae are primary locomotory organelles that propel bacteria through fluid media.
Statement II: The basal body of a bacterial flagellum is the longest portion that extends into the extracellular environment.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the function of pili and fimbriae
Pili and fimbriae are non-motile bacterial surface structures involved in attachment to surfaces, rocks, and host tissues, rather than cell locomotion.

Step 2: Evaluation of flagellar structural domains
In bacterial flagella, the filament constitutes the longest segment extending from the cell surface outward, while the basal body remains anchored within the cell envelope.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements are scientifically incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q11 - Mechanisms of active transport across plasma membrane

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Active transport is an energy-dependent process in which ATP is utilized to pump molecules against their concentration gradient.
Statement II: Neutral solutes require carrier proteins and ATP hydrolysis to cross the lipid bilayer down their concentration gradient.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of active transport characteristics
Active transport moves ions or solutes uphill from lower to higher concentration, directly utilizing metabolic energy in the form of ATP, as exemplified by the Na+/K+ pump.

Step 2: Evaluation of neutral solute permeability
Neutral solutes move freely across the lipid bilayer along their concentration gradient by simple passive diffusion without requiring carrier proteins or cellular energy expenditure.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is true, whereas the second statement is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q12 - Microtubule arrangements in eukaryotic cilia and centrioles

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The axoneme of eukaryotic cilia possesses nine peripheral triplet microtubules and no central microtubules.
Statement II: Both cilia and flagella emerge from centriole-like structures called basal bodies.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of ciliary axoneme ultrastructure
The axoneme of eukaryotic cilia and flagella displays a 9+2 array consisting of nine peripheral doublet microtubules and two central singlet microtubules; peripheral triplets are characteristic of centrioles.

Step 2: Evaluation of ciliary and flagellar origins
Both cilia and flagella develop from specialized centriole-derived structures termed basal bodies.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is false, whereas the second statement is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q13 - Functional coordination of the endomembrane system

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The endomembrane system includes endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles because their functions are coordinated.
Statement II: Mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes are not considered part of the endomembrane system as their functions are not coordinated with these organelles.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the constituents of the endomembrane system
The endomembrane system specifically comprises the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vacuoles due to the tight coordination of synthesis, packaging, and trafficking of materials between them.

Step 2: Evaluation of the excluded organelles
Because the metabolic and energy-transducing functions of mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes operate independently of this secretory pathway, they are excluded from the endomembrane system.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements accurately explain the functional definition and constituent boundaries of the eukaryotic endomembrane system.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q14 - Genome structure of mitochondria and chloroplasts

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The mitochondrial matrix possesses multiple linear DNA molecules packaged with basic histone proteins.
Statement II: Chloroplast stroma lacks ribosomes and depends entirely on cytoplasmic ribosomes for all enzyme synthesis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of mitochondrial DNA architecture
The mitochondrial matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule devoid of histone proteins, characteristic of prokaryotic-type genetic material.

Step 2: Evaluation of chloroplast translation machinery
The stroma of chloroplasts contains its own circular DNA and functional 70S ribosomes, allowing it to synthesize a portion of its own proteins autonomously.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both statements are scientifically incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q15 - Polarity and vesicle movement in Golgi apparatus

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Materials packaged in the form of vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the convex cis face of the Golgi apparatus.
Statement II: Proteins leave the Golgi apparatus from the cis face without undergoing any post-translational modifications in the cisternae.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of vesicle entry at the Golgi cis face
Transport vesicles budding from the endoplasmic reticulum dock and fuse with the convex cis (forming) face of the Golgi apparatus.

Step 2: Evaluation of vesicle modification and departure
Proteins are chemically modified within the Golgi cisternae and are subsequently sorted and discharged from the concave trans (maturing) face, not the cis face.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is true, whereas the second statement is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_STATEMENT_Q16 - Ion concentration and transport across the tonoplast

Statement II: The tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of vacuolar ion concentration
In plant cells, the concentration of various ions is significantly higher inside the vacuolar sap than in the surrounding cytoplasm.

Step 2: Evaluation of tonoplast transport activity
The single membrane delimiting the vacuole (tonoplast) actively pumps ions and solutes uphill against concentration gradients into the vacuolar lumen.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is false, whereas the second statement is true.
